rating_explained: The Washington Examiner asserts three things: Araghchi's 'doomsday war' warning on NBC's Meet the Press, Trump's Saturday rejection of Iran's ceasefire offer, and the Wall Street Journal's report that Trump expects to resume bombing after the midterms. The New York Post independently confirms the core quote from the Sunday Meet the Press interview — 'We stand firm in the face of any aggression against us, even when it comes to a doomsday war... At the same time, we are ready for diplomacy' — and confirms Trump's rejection of the overture, describing the seven-day proposal as involving unfreezing roughly $12 billion in Iranian assets, ending the blockade, and easing sanctions in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The National News Desk corroborates the WSJ report, writing that the Journal broke the news Friday night citing U.S. officials that Trump told aides he expects U.S. bombing to resume after November's midterms, and that Trump told reporters Saturday the deal 'would not be acceptable.' Every element of the trending claim is supported by two independent named outlets, and the WSJ component is correctly presented as a report attributed to the Journal's U.S.-official sources rather than as a confirmed fact.
trending_claim: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned Iran is prepared for a 'doomsday war' after Trump publicly rejected Tehran's ceasefire offer Saturday (a halt to Hormuz attacks plus resumed nuclear talks in exchange for lifting the U.S. naval blockade); the WSJ reports Trump told aides he expects to resume intensive bombing after the midterms.

All major elements check out against two independent outlets.

rating_explained: Newsmax asserts the Senate rejected the Iran war powers resolution 50-49 on Thursday, with four named Republicans voting for it and Fetterman as the lone Democratic no vote. NPR (via WAMC) confirms the resolution failed 49 to 50 and names the same four Republicans — Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, Rand Paul, Thom Tillis — as voting with Democrats, with Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman 'the lone Democrat to vote no.' Reuters (via SRN News) independently confirms the identical 50-49 tally, the same four Republican yes votes, and Fetterman as the single Democrat voting against. The only flaw is the claim's 'needed 51 votes' explanation: because 99 of 100 senators voted, a simple majority of 50 would have sufficed for passage, so the measure actually fell one yes vote short of 50, not 51. The vote count, the four Republican names, and Fetterman's unique Democratic opposition are all confirmed by two wire outlets; only the threshold number is slightly off.
trending_claim: The Senate defeated the Iran war powers resolution 50-49 on Thursday: four Republicans (Rand Paul, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, Thom Tillis) voted for it, Democrat John Fetterman was the lone Democrat voting against it, and the measure died because it needed 51 votes.
